newsitem.title: USA: Full recovery in aluminum demand delayed - Spector. [CORRECTED 17:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Full recovery in aluminum demand delayed - Spector. [CORRECTED 17:29 GMT]

text.p: Following an upward (corrects from downward) revision of first-half global (corrects from U.S.) primary aluminum inventory shrinkage, the metal's global growth forecast has been slashed by two-thirds, industry analyst Stewart Spector said in his latest Aluminum Industry Service newsletter.
In addition, June saw an unusually large inventory drawdown by U.S. end users.
"Thus, June U.S. ingot shipments to customers, who account for one-third of the world's consumption of primary, were sluggish," Spector said.
With lower than expected first half ingot shipments, "we now look for only a 1 percent year-to-year increase from last year - 18.9 million tons compared to 18.7 million in 1995."
Spector had forecast a rise of 3 percent initially.
"The downward forecast revisions now puts off the likelihood of a full recovery in aluminum demand until sometime in the first half of 1997," Spector added.
But lower-than-expected demand should also delay the restart of idled capacity thus doing "very little to alter the probably tight supply/demand situation we envision for the period 1998/2000."
Meanwhile new U.S. bookings for mill products in June, July and August have rebounded and, excluding can sheet, are now at their best levels since 1994, Spector said.
